accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC 2013 KS1 working scientifically ('gathering and recording data to help in answering questions'; 'observing closely, using simple equipment'): the lab and text use exactly those three record types from the topic evidence (simple table, tally chart, labelled drawing). Tally convention (four upright strokes, fifth across, a 'gate' of 5) matches the NCETM/NC Year 2 statistics usage. Lab data checked in code: VISITS gives robin 5, sparrow 4, pigeon 3 (12 birds, last one a pigeon); HEIGHTS 2, 5, 9 cm on a 0-10 cm ruler, growth 9 - 2 = 7 cm as the text says; the snail's shell, feelers (tentacles, eye spot at the tip) and muscular foot are correct names for ages 5-7. Parameterised items checked at range corners: p2 5g + r (5..19), p3 d (1..5, heights 3..11 cm), m2 5 + r (6..9), m7 k (1..4).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented KS1 recording slips (ASE/PSTT 'Working scientifically in the primary classroom' and teacher guidance on tally charts): relying on memory instead of recording as you go (step 1 prediction 'just remember', challenge tags mem/later, m5); drawing 5 strokes in a row or misreading a gate as 4 or 1 (step 2 prediction, tags gate4/gate1, m1); writing a reading in the wrong row (table step feedback for a value from an earlier day, tags row/any, m6); reading the top of the ruler instead of the plant (the 10 card gets its own message); a picture with no labels (step 4 prediction 'lots of colours', p5); and answering from a hunch such as the biggest bird or the one seen last instead of the record (step 5 prediction, ASK feedback for pigeon, tags first/last, p4, m8).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrecord is about choosing and making a record during an enquiry: match a question to tally/table/drawing, tally birds live as they land (the next bird only appears after the right mark), write ruler readings into the right day's row while the earlier plant disappears, label a drawing with label lines, then answer the original question from the record. flagtally reads and builds pictograms from finished votes, flagobsvs separates observations from guesses, flagscale is about reading scales accurately; none choose a record type or record events as they happen. 6-shingle similarity is at most 2.3% (with flag_nline.js) against every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea by doing: picking a drawing for 'how many birds' gets 'a drawing shows what a bird looks like, not how many came'; tallying shows the fifth mark crossing the four and the narration says 'That is a gate'; on day 3 the earlier plant is gone but the table still holds 2 cm, so the value of recording is seen, then named; a label dropped on the wrong spot gets a describing hint, not the answer; in the last step the biggest bird (pigeon, which also came last) is the tempting pick, and the tally shows it has the fewest marks.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: best record to count birds ('a drawing of each bird' / 'just remember'; the matching step only accepts the tally); how to show 5 ('5 lines in a row'; the chart draws four and a fifth across); a good science drawing ('lots of colours'; only labels with lines complete the step); which bird came most ('the pigeon: it is the biggest' / 'the bird that came last'; the tally shows pigeon 3, robin 5).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct wrong-answer messages in why(), each naming the slip: draw (one drawing shows a car, not how many), mem (you will forget), gate4 and gate1 (the gate is 5 marks, not 4 or 1), row (each day its own row), any (numbers dotted about are hard to compare), count (one beetle, nothing to tally), num (one number cannot show legs or wings), first and last (order does not change the count), fill (a record is not to fill space), later (write it as soon as you see it). The matching, table, label and answer steps add their own per-choice messages (PICKWHY, write(), PARTS hints, ASK.why).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience (kid and adult readability within limits). Ages 5-7 wording: sentences of 4-12 words, everyday words (marks, gate, row, label, guess), curriculum terms introduced plainly (data = what you count, measure or see; tally chart; table; labelled drawing; label line). Lab buttons are one or two words (+ Robin, 5 cm, Spot 1, shell); every canvas word is 13-22 px bold on a pale card, and long lines shrink to fit at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases, explanation overlap under 12% with every lesson). Kid paragraphs: why record; tally charts and gates; tables for measurements; labelled drawings and answering from the record. Adult paragraphs: KS1 statement and key words; named common mistakes; why the choice of record is part of the enquiry; what each lab step does. Each lab step text is one or two short sentences of instruction.

mobile.evidence: Before/after Show me screenshots of all six steps on iPhone 13 (390 px) and 360 px Android in light and dark, and desktop. First pass clipped the 'How many of each bird…' card at 360 px, let the ruler's 10 mark run under the title card, overlapped snail labels on the shell and drew the feelers in dark ink on the dark theme; fixed by shrinking long card text to fit, lowering the ruler base, placing each label at its own spot outside the drawing, and using the theme line colour. Tally rows are 55+ px tall full-width tap targets; record cards about 110 x 150 px; number cards 52+ px; control buttons wrap below.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: 'Record with a tally chart', 'Add a tally mark for robin', 'Write 5 cm for day 1', 'Pick the label shell' then 'Put the label on spot 1', 'Answer Robin'; the label step also accepts drag or tap-then-tap. tell() updates the canvas aria-label and the visible narration after every action (e.g. 'One mark for robin. Robin: 5. That is a gate: 4 marks and 1 across.'). walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes, no console errors. Canvas text is dark ink on pale cards in both themes.
